title: Calling :q while there is a scheduled function that calls 'vsplit | q' causes a core dump

labels.name: bug-crash
labels.description: issue reporting a crash or segfault

body:
<!-- Before reporting: search existing issues and check the FAQ. -->

- `nvim --version`:
```
NVIM v0.5.0-dev+1260-ga6504ec33
Build type: RelWithDebInfo
LuaJIT 2.0.5
Compilation: /usr/bin/cc -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 -march=x86-64 -mtune=generic -O2 -pipe -fno-plt -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=1 -O2 -g -Og -g -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Wno-unused-parameter -Wstrict-prototypes -std=gnu99 -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wmissing-prototypes -Wimplicit-fallthrough -Wvla -fstack-protector-strong -fno-common -fdiagnostics-color=auto -DINCLUDE_GENERATED_DECLARATIONS -D_GNU_SOURCE -DNVIM_MSGPACK_HAS_FLOAT32 -DNVIM_UNIBI_HAS_VAR_FROM -DMIN_LOG_LEVEL=3 -I/home/apple/.cache/yay/neovim-git/src/build/config -I/home/apple/.cache/yay/neovim-git/src/neovim-git/src -I/usr/include -I/home/apple/.cache/yay/neovim-git/src/build/src/nvim/auto -I/home/apple/.cache/yay/neovim-git/src/build/include
Compiled by apple

   system vimrc file: "$VIM/sysinit.vim"
  fall-back for $VIM: "/usr/share/nvim"
```
- `vim -u DEFAULTS` (version: ) behaves differently? N/A afaik
- Operating system/version:
Arch Linux x86_64   5.11.13-arch1-1
glibc 2.33-4
- Terminal name/version:
zsh 5.8.1
- `$TERM`:
alacritty

### Steps to reproduce using `nvim -u NORC`

```vim
nvim -u NORC --cmd "lua vim.schedule(function() vim.cmd('vsplit | q') end)" +q
nvim -u NORC --cmd "lua vim.schedule(function() vim.cmd('vsplit | q') end) vim.cmd('q')" also works
```

### Actual behaviour
Neovim coredumps somewhere in libuv.
### Expected behaviour
Neovim quits normally.

There isn't usually a reason to be calling `:q` right after startup but in my case I'm using the `vsplit | q` to force certain plugins to load early and I'm using `+q` to benchmark my config startup with hyperfine. (As an aside, is there a way to quit w/o finishing scheduled commands first? I don't care too much about how long the commands take, but I am interested in the time it takes to schedule them)
